content: St. John’s wort, certain antidepressants such as selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) like fluoxetine and paroxetine, and serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs) like duloxetine and venlafaxine, among others, can interact with this medication. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911). If the situation is less critical, contact a poison control center without delay. U.S. residents can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in May 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. This medication may increase serotonin levels and, in rare cases, lead to a serious condition known as serotonin syndrome or serotonin toxicity. The risk of this condition is higher if you are taking other drugs that also increase serotonin levels. Inform your doctor or pharmacist about all the medications you are taking, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal products. Before taking alosetron, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the way your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications, such as fluvoxamine and viloxazine, may affect the removal of alosetron from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Additionally, the risk of severe complications from constipation increases if you are taking other drugs that may cause constipation. The risk of serotonin syndrome or toxicity increases if you are also taking other drugs that elevate serotonin levels. Examples include street drugs like MDMA (ecstasy), St. John’s wort, and certain antidepressants such as SSRIs (e.g., fluoxetine, paroxetine) and SNRIs (e.g., duloxetine, venlafaxine). If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
